Cyber Attack Disrupts Operations Across Egypt’s Cable & Satellite Industry

Cairo, June 13 – A large-scale cyber attack has struck Egypt’s cable and satellite industry, disrupting operations at broadcasting centers and technical sites across multiple regions, industry sources said Thursday.

The incident, believed to be a ransomware attack targeting IT systems, began late Wednesday and continued into Thursday, affecting several firms including NileSatCom, Delta Cable Networks, and Horizon Satellite Services. The Egyptian Cable & Satellite Association confirmed in a statement that “core broadcasting and scheduling systems have been compromised, resulting in intermittent outages and delays in content delivery.”

Workers at affected firms reported being locked out of scheduling, billing, and engineering platforms. “We are unable to access our internal networks or support systems,” said Ahmed Fathy, a technician at NileSatCom. “Most of the team has been sent home while we wait for instructions.”

Industry representatives declined to specify the number of companies impacted but described the event as “unprecedented in scale.” Initial assessments by cybersecurity analysts suggest the attack is ongoing, with ransom demands issued in encrypted messages to company administrators.

“We are working closely with cybersecurity consultants and law enforcement to contain the breach and restore systems,” said Laila Mansour, spokesperson for the Egyptian Cable & Satellite Association. “Our priority is to protect sensitive data and resume normal operations as soon as possible.”

Union officials expressed concern for the workforce. “Hundreds of employees are affected, with many unable to perform their duties or access payroll systems,” said Ibrahim Khalil, head of the National Broadcast Workers Union.

As of Thursday afternoon, companies reported partial restoration of some analog systems, but digital operations remain severely limited. The association advised member firms to implement additional security protocols pending further updates.
